## Natural history notes

A small gilled mushroom characterized by its variable tan to orange-brown cap, widely spaced pale gills, slender fibrous stem, and highly changeable appearance as it dries or ages. In Florida, it is found on soil, leaf litter, mossy ground, lawns, pine flatwoods, hammocks, and other wooded or grassy habitats where it grows in association with plant roots. It is a mycorrhizal fungus, exchanging nutrients with nearby plants, and is often called the “deceiver” because its color and shape can vary enough to make identification difficult.
